rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment tests a baseline RNA-only singleprofile model with PCA encoding. It clarifies the performance of a simple unimodal approach, establishing a reference point before exploring multimodal or more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 48.5% accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (same RNA encoder, no image data), isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) with exploitation (using proven RNA encoder), and addresses key uncertainty about whether multiprofile improves performance.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001, 0.4849). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 (config_005) further improves accuracy while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of encoder alternatives with exploitation of the promising multiprofile/avgpool combination.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and multiprofile achieve 0.65 accuracy (config_005). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline using avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation of the current best RNA encoder with exploration of multimodal potential, a critical design choice with high uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and SCVI encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods on RNA-only models with SCVI encoder, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only models with transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.6529 accuracy) outperform others. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (config_009) while retaining transformer aggregation could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which remains uncertain despite scvi_n200's prior success. This comparison directly addresses a key design choice with high potential impact, balancing exploitation of effective aggregation methods with exploration of new encoders.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.652970) outperform other configurations. This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline, using transformer aggregation (a key factor in config_006's success) and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal inputs while maintaining proven RNA and aggregation choices, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 achieve higher accuracy (0.687) than rna_only models. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget to further refine the top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l in config_033, which could improve performance by leveraging a more powerful vision transformer. It isolates the effect of the image encoder while keeping other high-performing components fixed, maximizing the chance to surpass the current best accuracy with the final experiment.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (config_039: 0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation but weighted fusion, which could isolate the effect of RNA encoder choice. While scgpt has lower performance in single-task settings, combining it with strong image features and fusion might yield unexpected improvements, providing critical insight into RNA encoder impact.
